newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Bach Ho crude term talks extended due to deadlock.
newsitem.headline: Bach Ho crude term talks extended due to deadlock.

text.p: State-owned Petrovietnam Trading Co. (Petechim) has extended its term Bach Ho crude price negotiations for another week, due to a deadlock with its buyers, traders said on Monday.
Petechim was to have made a decision by Friday on the Bach Ho term official selling price (OSP) for its six-month contracts which begin in October.
But Petechim was unable to come to an agreement with its term buyers on the premium in the OSP, traders said.
Starting October, Petechim will use a new formula to calculate its OSP, using the three week average of Platt's daily quotes and APPI bi-weekly quotes, with a premium then added.
This is the first time that Petechim has adjusted its Bach Ho OSP formula, since the crude was sold in 1989.
At present, the Bach Ho OSP is set using just the APPI, with a premium added.
But traders said that the deadlock was due to Petechim maintaining its offer of a premium of 85 cents per barrel over the Platt's and APPI average.
Buyers, meanwhile, were looking at a premium of 60 cents.
The buyers had initially bid a premium of 40 to 50 cents, but had moved up their prices to narrow the gap between the bid and offer.
Bach Ho output is around 170,000 barrels-per-day, most of which is sold on term to Japanese trading houses and majors Shell, Caltex, Exxon and Mobil.
Petechim's Bach Ho crude contracts with its term customers are renewed every six months, following the six-monthly review of the OSP.
Despite earlier complaints that the new Bach Ho OSP formula will result in higher prices, none of the term customers have yet indicated an official intention to withdraw.
"But they will only decide after the term price is set" said a Japanese trader.
